Charlie Speechley, our evergreen walker, was not feeling up to the mark and so had to miss "Our Open," much to his regret. Few members know that Charlie is also (or has been) an accomplished swimmer and diver, and some years ago very narrowly missed his Olympic Colours.

Congratulations to CHARLIE SPEECHLEY who had his 82nd birthday recently and is still very active indeed - and in a competitive way at that! He confides that he covered 1,100 miles in training and racing last year!

Ernest Neville (88 years) Charlie Speechley (83) and 1932 Olympic champion Tommy GREEN (77) - the youngest were still in single figures! In the Vets AC Championship held at Battersea Park on July 7th over 3,200 metres, Dave McMullen came home 2nd in 15:30 behind K.Livermore (Woodford Green).15:09. John Bromley was 5th in 15:59 and 12th was evergreen Charlie Speechley, 86 years old and spritely enough to clock 25:29.
Charlie Speechley, our oldest member, was involved in sport before World War I and took part in the trial for the 1908 Olympic Games at Diving!

Eighty-seven year old CHARLIE SPEECHLEY also made the trip to Toronto. He lined up for a 200 metre race against Fritz Schreiber (Sweden), a mere lad of 82, and Duncan (Tartan Flash) MacLean the 90 year old Scot.

Our two "supervets" Duncan Maclean and Charlie Speechley were in action at Norbiton track on 29th May. In addition to the Banstead Trophy events there was a Veterans' Sprint Handicap, and our pair were seen in action again.

Sixty-five members turned up for the A.G.M. in September, amongst them Charlie Speechley who will soon be 80 years old. Charlie had made the two hour journey to Wimbledon from his Eastcote home to attend, changing buses and trains several times.
By my reckoning Charlie Speechley must be over 60, Charlie Jones over 40, Tom Carter almost 95, Doub getting on for 35 but none looked any older than when I joined the Club in 1948.
Our oldest member, Charlie Speechley, who will be ninety by the time this is in print, recently fell from a ladder in his garden causing very bad lacerations to his legs and breaking two ribs.

Other Belgravians at the Southern Vets were Dave McMullen, who was first in the 2B 3,000 metres Walk with 15:08.0, and Charlie Speechley who placed second in the 5B 100 metres - 0.5 behind the 'Tartan Flash' Duncan McLean.
